topicName: Table Partitioning: Range, List, Hash, and Key
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"MySQL Table Partitioning: Range, List, Hash, and Key"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Table partitioning in MySQL allows you to divide large tables into smaller, more manageable pieces called partitions based on a set of rules. This technique can drastically improve query performance, simplify maintenance operations, and optimize storage utilization for massive datasets."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Range Partitioning"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Range partitioning divides data based on columns whose values fall within specified continuous ranges. It is most commonly used with date or timestamp columns, such as archiving logs by year."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE employees (
    id INT NOT NULL,
    fname VARCHAR(30),
    hired DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '1970-01-01'
)
PARTITION BY RANGE (YEAR(hired)) (
    PARTITION p0 VALUES LESS THAN (1990),
    PARTITION p1 VALUES LESS THAN (2000),
    PARTITION p2 VALUES LESS THAN (2010),
    PARTITION p3 VALUES LESS THAN MAXVALUE
);"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. List Partitioning"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"List partitioning is similar to range partitioning, but the partition is selected based on columns matching one of a set of discrete values rather than a continuous range."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE traffic_logs (
    log_id INT NOT NULL,
    region_code INT,
    log_message VARCHAR(255)
)
PARTITION BY LIST (region_code) (
    PARTITION p_north VALUES IN (1, 4, 7),
    PARTITION p_south VALUES IN (2, 5, 8),
    PARTITION p_east VALUES IN (3, 6, 9)
);"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Hash Partitioning"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Hash partitioning is used to ensure an even distribution of data among a predetermined number of partitions. You supply an expression based on the column value, and MySQL applies a hashing algorithm to determine the target partition."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id INT NOT NULL,
    customer_name VARCHAR(50)
)
PARTITION BY HASH (customer_id)
PARTITIONS 4;"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Key Partitioning"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Key partitioning is similar to hash partitioning, except that the hashing is supplied by MySQL server and the partitioning key can be one or more columns, typically including the primary key."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE users (
    user_id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(50)
)
PARTITION BY KEY (user_id)
PARTITIONS 2;"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Maintenance and Best Practices"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always include the partitioning key in your primary or unique keys if you define them."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use partition pruning by including the partition column in your WHERE clauses to maximize performance."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly drop old partitions using 'ALTER TABLE table_name DROP PARTITION partition_name;' to optimize storage for time-series data."}]
